My name is Veronica Blair and I'm the Policy Manager with the Community Standards Department.
This hearing is to consider amendments to the sign regulations and appendix A of the zoning by law as well as complementary amendments to the development applications fee by law.
The sign regulations provide requirements for all signs on private property within Saskatoon.
Administration recently reviewed the regulations pertaining primarily to two sign types digital signs and project development signs.
Digital signs include any electronic sign panel where content can be changed digitally and project development signs include temporary signage used to advertise a construction or development project.
The objectives of the regulation review were to address community concerns related to traffic safety sign clutter and impacts to adjacent land uses from the sign types.
Best practice research and community feedback was used to develop the proposed amendments.
Key amendments include providing detailed standards on sign brightness to mitigate impacts at night.
Specifying minimum setbacks for digital signs from residential uses and natural areas.
Incorporating traffic safety best practices for sign placement.

Updating permitting requirements defining temporary signs based on project type and including removal requirements for said signs and aligned aligning permit fees with administrative review times to ensure the sign program remains fully cost recovery.
The engagement process with residents stakeholder groups in the sign industry as outlined in appendix three generated a diverse range of perspectives on the regulations.
Through the public survey residents expressed concerns with the brightness of existing digital panels their impact to nearby residential areas at night and the potential for driver distraction.
Through direct engagement the sign industry and business community confirm the importance of digital advertising as a cost effective and impactful form of advertising.

In administration's view the proposed amendments provide appropriate balance between addressing resident concerns and keeping digital advertising as a viable medium through clear and consistent regulations.
